member.name: T:JCass_Core.Engineering.RuleParser
member.summary:
Parses and evaluates conditional rule statements against data rows.
Supported grammar (recursive, one connector type per group):
expression := group ( connector group )* // all connectors at one level must be the same group := '[' expression ']' | comparison comparison := identifier op literal | identifier IN '(' string_list ')' op := >= | <= | > | < | == | = | != | <> literal := number | 'string' connector := AND | OR
Examples:
rut_mean < 6 AND adt < 5000 rut_mean < 6 AND surf_class IN ('CS','SLURRY','OTHER','CONC') [adt > 5000] OR [rut_mean < 6 AND age < 15]
Mixed AND/OR at the same level without bracketing is rejected at parse time. Each rule is parsed once at construction and evaluated through a small AST in the hot path, so the parser is suitable for Monte Carlo simulations with many evaluations against the same rule set.
Each rule is identified by a caller-supplied string label (e.g. a cohort name). Rules are evaluated in the order in which they are enumerated by the constructor argument, and the label of the first matching rule is returned. Duplicate labels are rejected at construction time.

member.param: Ordered sequence of (label, rule statement) pairs. Labels must be unique and non-empty.
How to react to null cell values during evaluation.
member.exception: Thrown if the collection is empty, contains a null/empty or duplicate label, or any rule fails to parse.

member.name: M:JCass_Core.JFunctions.SShapedModelHelper.GetSCurveProgressionIncrement(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Gets an increment for distress progression following an S-curve such that an incremental model will reach 100% distress when the years since initiation equals parameter 'periodsToReach100Percent'. This implementation is such that the inflection point at which the increment reaches a maximum (after which it reduces) occurs at 30% of the 'periodsToReach100Percent'. This gives a faster initial growth until about 30% of the time to reach 100% cracks, and then a longer taper down period to reach 100% This method was calibrated using trial and error checking with R and gives a nice S-shape.
member.remarks: For this method to give a nice curve, the increments needs to be utilised in an INCREMENTAL model that starts from zero up to values of periodsToReach100Percent or less. You must increment from zero and proceed in increments of 1 period at a time. If you jump from period zero to 5 it means that you are not properly accumulating distress and this will then NOT give an S-curve
member.param: Number of periods (usually years) until 100% distress is reached
Number of periods since distress initiation
member.returns: The increment, in percent, at the specified 'periodsSinceInitiation' to give a cumulative S-curve that will reach 100 when periodsSinceInitiation equals periodsToReach100Percent

member.summary: Provides functionality to represent a linear regression model with specified coefficients, and an optional piecewise linear model to calculate the standard deviation of the residuals as a function of a predictor variable. The Predict method calculates the predicted value based on the input variables and the coefficients, while the PredictResidualStdDev method calculates the standard deviation of the residuals based on the predictor variable using the piecewise linear model if it is defined.

member.name: M:JCass_Core.Statistics.LinearRegressionModel.Predict(System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,System.Double})
member.summary: Gets a prediction from the linear regression model based on the provided input variables. The inputVariables dictionary should contain values for all the predictor variables used in the model, with keys matching the variable names in the coefficients dictionary (excluding the '(Intercept)' term). The method calculates the predicted value by summing the intercept and the products of each coefficient with its corresponding input variable value. If any required input variable is missing, an exception is thrown.
member.param: Input variables for the prediction. Keys must match the coefficient names in the model (excluding the '(Intercept)' term).
member.returns: The predicted value based on the input variables and model coefficients.
member.exception: Thrown if the inputVariables dictionary is null.
Thrown if any required input variable is missing.
member.remarks: Performance: O(n) where n is the number of coefficients in the model.

member.name: M:JCass_Core.Statistics.LinearRegressionModel.PredictResidualStdDev(System.Double)
member.summary: Predicts the standard deviation of the residuals for a given predictor value using the piecewise linear model. This allows the model to account for heteroscedasticity by providing different residual standard deviation estimates based on the level of the predictor variable. If the piecewise linear model is not defined, an exception is thrown.
member.param: The predictor value for which to estimate the residual standard deviation.
member.returns: The predicted standard deviation of the residuals corresponding to the specified predictor value.
member.exception: Thrown if the model does not have a piecewise linear model defined for residual standard deviation.
member.remarks: Uses the PieceWiseLinearModel.GetValue() method which has O(log n) performance with binary search.

The random error is drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation equal to the predicted residual standard deviation for the given predictor value. member.name: T:JCass_Core.Statistics.LogisticModel
member.summary: Represents a logistic regression model using coefficients exported from an R glm(..., family = binomial(link = "logit")) fit.

remarks.para: This class implements the standard logistic regression prediction equations:

item.description: The coefficient dictionary must contain an intercept term named exactly (Intercept).
This class assumes there are no interaction terms such as a:b.
This class assumes there are no transformed terms such as log(x), poly(...), splines, factor expansions, or offsets.
Each non-intercept coefficient name must exactly match a key in the predictor-value dictionary passed to prediction methods.
If any required predictor is missing during prediction, an exception is thrown.
Extra entries in the predictor-value dictionary are ignored.
This class is intended for models fitted with the logit link. It is not suitable for probit, cloglog, multinomial, ordinal, or other model forms.

remarks.para: The probability calculation uses a numerically stable implementation to reduce overflow risk for large positive or negative logits.

member.name: M:JCass_Core.Utils.HelperMethods.GetFinancialYear(System.DateTime,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the calendar year for the financial year start in which a date falls. A very simple helper function. If the date has a month later than the financial year start, then the financial year is the same as the year's date. But if the month is earlier or the same as the month in which the financial year ends, then the financial year is the year before that of the date.
member.param: Date to evaluate
Month in which the financial year ends (at the end of this month). E.g. if financial year ends 30 June, then enter 6
member.returns: Integer representing the financial year's starting calendar year
member.example: If date is 20-Feb-2023, then the date falls in the financial year that started in July 2022 and ends at 30 June 2023. Thus return value is 2022
If date is 20-Dec-2023, then the date falls in the financial year that started in July 2023 and ends at 30 June 2024. Thus return value is 2023
If date is 1-July-2023, then the date falls in the financial year that started in July 2023 and ends at 30 June 2024. Thus return value is 2023
If date is 30-Jun-2023, then the date falls in the financial year that started in July 2022 and ends at 30 June 2023. Thus return value is 2022
